recentItems.title: Two rescued in Nepal 10 days after disaster
recentItems.description:
Two people, including a Chinese national, have been rescued 10 days after a glacial collapse caused a catastrophic flash flood disaster on the China-Nepal border. Lu Haitao, a Chinese national, became trapped in a 225-metre tunnel at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Rasuwa district. He was rescued on Saturday by the Nepalese army. Aside from showing mild signs of hypothermia, Lu had no visible injuries and his vitals were stable. Another survivor, 64-year-old Chandra Shrestha, was found alive in the debris of her partially buried home. She was airlifted to a hospital in Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu, for treatment.

recentItems.title: How Starbucks Malaysia changed the game for deaf baristas
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

A decade ago, Starbucks Malaysia launched an ambitious experiment to create meaningful career opportunities for the nation’s deaf community. The initiative evolved from offering entry-level jobs into establishment of the world’s first Starbucks Signing Store in Kuala Lumpur. Now, deaf employees are even able to build long-term careers and advance to management roles. As the pilot project changed lives, the concept was expanded to 26 stores around the world. But despite the programme’s success, major communication and educational barriers remain for disabled people hoping to enter the mainstream workforce.

recentItems.title: Why does Hong Kong struggle to ease competition among its youth?
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

More on Hong Kong education: https://sc.mp/19c5a5

Since Hong Kong’s handover in 1997, the government has sought to transform the city’s education system from a colonial system focused on memorisation and exam pressure, and towards a more holistic development meant to foster lifelong learning. But decades on, competition has only grown stronger among Hong Kong’s young students, extending beyond the confines of the classroom and into their extracurricular activities. What are the factors driving this competition and what is being done to ease pressure on pupils?

recentItems.title: Hong Kong caps access to Sai Kung trail with reservation scheme
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Read more: https://sc.mp/4e43e4

Hong Kong authorities are capping access to a popular Sai Kung trail starting Saturday. Visitor numbers on the coastal Po Pin Chau section of the High Island Geo Trail will be limited to 2,000 per day on weekends and public holidays. Hikers planning to visit during these times will need to register in advance. The initiative marks Hong Kong’s first countryside crowd-control scheme.

recentItems.title: Global Education Summit kicks off in Hong Kong
recentItems.description:
Next-generation skills that children need to outpace artificial intelligence and thrive in an ever-shifting job market are among the critical topics being discussed at the first Global Education Summit in Hong Kong. The two-day event, co-organised by SCMP Learn and HSBC Premier, brings together educators, policymakers and C-suite executives to discuss important issues concerning the future of education. The event also features exhibition booths from more than 40 top second and post-secondary institutions, giving attendees advice on what admissions officers are looking for beyond good grades.

recentItems.title: How this Mong Kok fish ball shop keeps its prices low
recentItems.description:
After six decades of supplying restaurants across Hong Kong with high-quality, locally made fish balls, Kau Kei Food Factory is now also selling directly to customers – at a fraction of the price. Owner Anita Lee pivoted the business in 2025, opening Kau Kei’s first retail outlet in Mong Kok. The move was to let customers buy its signature fish balls without the restaurant mark-up, and to raise the brand’s profile in the heart of the city.

recentItems.title: Nepali survivor recounts escape from flood-hit tunnel
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Read more: https://sc.mp/dfd2f0

Rescuers in Nepal continue trying to reach hundreds of workers believed trapped inside tunnels at hydropower plant projects at the nation’s border with China. Authorities estimate that about 900 people remain trapped inside six hydropower plants in Nepal, where a glacier collapse last Wednesday sent a giant wave of mud, rock and water barrelling through mountain valleys, killing more than 1,200 people. Several hundred workers have been rescued from the tunnels, including 32-year-old Dhan Bahadur Tamang, who says he is grateful to have survived the disaster.

recentItems.title: Indonesians reportedly fought for Russia in Ukraine war
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Read more about this: https://sc.mp/62f8o

Indonesia is investigating reports that eight of its citizens who applied for civilian jobs were instead recruited to fight for Russia against Ukraine. Indonesia’s Coordinating Minister for Legal, Human Rights, Immigration and Corrections, Yusril Ihza Mahendra, said authorities are checking the identities and hiring processes of the individuals, who were allegedly lured by promises of high-paying, non-combat roles as well as fast-tracked Russian citizenship.

recentItems.title: Beauty consultant arrested for alleged aggressive sales tactics
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Hong Kong customs officers have arrested a woman on suspicion of using aggressive tactics to sell skincare products at a local beauty chain formerly operating under the Opatra London brand. The arrest of the 22-year-old beauty consultant brings the number of people apprehended in the case to three, after two managers linked to the brand were detained over similar tactics last month.
